basis: Defective regulation of inflammatory mediators causes the defining angioedema and urticaria; airway disease is not established as common.
Craniosynostosis and limb malformations define Carpenter syndrome; patent ductus arteriosus and cutis laxa each occur in 2/5; developmental delay only 1/5.
CNS developmental injury defines FAS; eye defects, ASD and joint/vertebral defects each 30-79%; dental defects also 30-79%, omitted by cap.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by shortening of the middle limb bones.
Tumour arises in testicular germ cells; reproductive tumour origin has no axis, and hormone production does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Oxidative phosphorylation defect; cardiomyopathy 9/9, anemia 7/7 and liver dysfunction 5/9; hearing loss 1/1 omitted given cap and sparse evidence.
Umbrella of lysosomal metabolic disorders; organ damage varies substantially by subtype, without a sufficiently uniform additional organ label.
Microcephaly and chorioretinal disease define the syndrome; scoliosis is frequent (30-79%).
Temple syndrome commonly causes central precocious puberty and metabolic abnormalities; motor/speech developmental delay affects over half.
Inherited photodermatosis; common ocular or neurologic damage is not established for this specifically mild dominant form.
Predominantly a craniofacial skeletal malformation syndrome; hypertelorism does not itself establish ocular damage; other organ defects are variable.
Carnitine-dependent fatty acid oxidation disorder; hepatic and muscle disease differ between CPT1A and CPT2 subtypes and are not uniform across the umbrella.
Inherited loss of ovarian endocrine function; additional organ involvement depends on the underlying syndrome.
Necrosis of the femoral head is the defining bone lesion; localized ischemia does not establish a separate vascular disease.
Broad chromosomal duplication syndrome with common developmental impairment across major subtypes; other structural organ anomalies depend on the duplicated region.
Glycogen metabolic disease with hepatomegaly 80-99% and fibrosis 30-79%; muscle weakness only 3/15 despite muscle enzyme deficiency.
Carcinoma originates in bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis.
Broad chromosomal deletion syndrome with common neurodevelopmental impairment; additional organ malformations vary with the deleted region.
Congenital cyst of the thyroid developmental tract; thyroid-associated origin supports the endocrine axis despite usually preserved hormone function.
Malignancy originates in exocrine pancreatic epithelium; exocrine pancreas belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Cranial nerve schwannoma; persistent hearing impairment from adjacent nerve compression occurs in approximately 50-70%.
Acute malignant proliferation of myeloid blood and marrow cells; leukemia alone does not establish an immune mechanism axis.
Neurovascular syndrome with peripheral neuropathy reported in 80-99%; erythema is transient, ulcers are occasional, and associated blood disorders are separate.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and infertility; reproductive dysfunction without established endocrine or other axis involvement.
Short-rib skeletal dysplasia causes common lethal pulmonary hypoplasia; brain defects are described as common (about 30% or more); renal and biliary lesions lack frequency evidence.
